answer: Each AI grader is assigned to a rotating orchard of peer validators that randomly select a small ripple of agents each epoch to audit grading signatures. Validators verify the opal proof of identity on each signature; any mismatch triggers a spot‑check audit requiring the suspect to present a fresh zero‑knowledge credential from its hardware enclave. Because the audit pool is unpredictable, an attacker must equip every potential validator with a valid credential, turning the cost from O(1) to linear in the number of agents and making Sybil floods prohibitively expensive.
